cards.text: This song is a psalm of Asaph, one of King David's worship leaders (1 Chronicles 16:4-5). He opens with a prayer to God, with no warm-up and no small talk. He goes STRAIGHT to it, friend.

cards.question: Asaph opens by asking God the same thing three different ways. What is he asking God not to be?

cards.text: Then Asaph points God to what's going on: "See how Your enemies rage, how Your foes have reared their heads." That's not a quiet prayer, friend, that's me yelling across the bakery when I see smoke pouring out of an oven.

cards.question: These raging enemies are scheming against God's people. Asaph says they scheme with ___.
The enemies have a plan, and Asaph quotes it. What do they say they want to do to Israel?

cards.text: That's a heavy plan, friend. And Asaph says it's not coming from just one nation.

cards.question: Asaph says the nations plotting against Israel can't agree on a plan.
These nations plot together with one mind and form an alliance. Who does Asaph say the alliance is against?

cards.text: Then Asaph names ten who are in on it, from Edom, Moab and Ammon to Philistia and Tyre, all the way to Assyria, lending strength to the sons of Lot (Lot was Abraham's nephew, Genesis 12:5). That's not an alliance, friend, that's a GROUP CHAT with only one topic.

Now Asaph pulls out the receipts, OLD ones: Midian, and Sisera and Jabin at the River Kishon. Back in Israel's past, Midian's army fled before Gideon, Israel's leader, and his three hundred men (Judges 7:19-22), and the LORD routed Sisera, commander of the army of Jabin, a king of Canaan (Judges 4:2, 15).

cards.question: Asaph brings up Midian, Sisera and Jabin. What is he asking God to do to today's enemies?

answers.text: Defeat them like He defeated those enemies
Send them back to their own lands

cards.text: Asaph does NOT soften it, friend: they perished at Endor and became like dung on the ground. Then he asks God to make today's nobles and princes like four leaders of Midian: Oreb and Zeeb (Judges 7:25), Zebah and Zalmunna (Judges 8:5).

cards.question: After naming Oreb, Zeeb, Zebah and Zalmunna, Asaph quotes some people who wanted to possess something for themselves. What was it?

cards.text: Then Asaph trades the history lesson for pictures, and the first one blows in on the wind.

cards.question: Asaph asks God to make the enemies like tumbleweed, like chaff before the wind.

cards.text: Like crumbs on my counter when I blow on them, FWOOSH, gone. Then the next picture: fire eating up a forest, and a flame setting the mountains ablaze.

cards.question: Just like that fire on the mountains, Asaph asks God to chase the enemies down and terrify them with His storm. What does he ask God to pursue them with?

cards.text: Then the prayer takes a turn I did NOT see coming. Asaph asks God to cover their faces with shame, and he says what it's for.

cards.question: Asaph asks God to cover the enemies' faces with shame, so that they may ___ the LORD's name.
After praying that the enemies seek the LORD's name, Asaph stops asking for them to be ashamed.

cards.text: Then Asaph gets to his very last line, and it's about what he wants them to know.

cards.question: Asaph ends his prayer with what he wants the enemies to know. What is it?

answers.text: That the LORD alone is Most High over all the earth
That Israel will rule over every nation on earth
That Asaph's prayers are always heard in heaven
